name: Learjet 40/45/70/75
summary: Last generation of Learjets (production ended 2022), widely used for charter and corporate travel in the US.

wings: Low swept wing with upturned winglets (blended on the 70/75)
engines: Two Honeywell TFE731-20/40 turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Slim fuselage with a long pointed nose and moderate-size windows
Two small ventral delta fins under the tail
tail: T-tail with a tall swept fin

tellTales: Pair of small ventral fins forming a V under the tail
Winglets on a sleek twinjet with a long pointed nose
T-tail on a tall swept fin

confusedWith.howToTell: The 40/45/70/75 is larger with winglets; the 35/36 has wingtip fuel tanks and the 31 is smaller with smaller windows.
The Learjet 45/75 has a long pointed nose, smaller windows and ventral fins; the Phenom 300 has very large windows and a rounded nose.
The Learjet 45 has winglets and ventral fins; the Beechjet/Hawker 400 has plain wingtips.
The Learjet 45 has winglets and a swept wing; the CJ series has plain wingtips on a straight wing.
The Learjet 55/60 has a shorter, stubbier wing with small winglets and a boxier cabin; the 45 has a longer-span wing with larger winglets and a more tapered fuselage.
